# SPI Device Module Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is a configurable SPI device. It provides four functional capabilities:

- **Generic SPI mode**: raw full-duplex byte transfer between an external SPI host and an internal memory buffer.
- **SPI flash mode**: emulation of a serial flash device, including hardware handling of status, JEDEC ID, SFDP, read commands, address mode tracking, and command upload.
- **SPI passthrough mode**: forwarding of SPI transactions to a downstream interface, with optional filtering, address/payload manipulation, and internal interception of selected commands.
- **TPM over SPI mode**: TPM-compatible SPI transaction handling with a dedicated TPM chip select.

At any time, the module operates in one of the three primary SPI modes. TPM mode is independently enabled and can be active together with any primary mode because it uses a separate chip select.

---

## 2. External Behavior and Interface

### 2.1 SPI Interface

The module provides an SPI interface consisting of:

- one SPI clock input,
- one primary active-low chip-select input,
- four bidirectional SPI data lines,
- one separate active-low TPM chip-select input.

The module shall treat a transaction as active while the primary chip select is low. Data transitions received while the chip select is high shall be ignored. For TPM transactions, the TPM chip select defines the active transaction instead.

The module shall support the standard SPI clock polarity and clock phase configurations. The active data sampling edge and output-driving edge shall follow the configured SPI mode.

The module shall support configurable bit order for received and transmitted bytes. Receive bit order and transmit bit order shall be independently selectable.

When the TPM function is enabled and the TPM chip select is low, the TPM function shall take ownership of the shared SPI data lines. During TPM transactions, the module shall receive TPM data on the host-to-device data line and drive the TPM response on the device-to-host data line. The remaining data lines shall not be driven by the TPM path.

### 2.2 Register and Memory Interface

The module shall be software-configurable through a TL-UL register interface. Software shall be able to:

- select the primary SPI mode,
- configure SPI timing and bit order,
- configure generic-mode buffer addresses and thresholds,
- configure flash-mode command information,
- read and write status and FIFO data,
- control and clear interrupts,
- access the internal SRAM buffer through the provided memory window.

The module shall provide status information to software, including FIFO empty/full conditions, buffer depths, interrupt status, and operational mode.

### 2.3 Reset and Initialization

At reset, the module shall return to its default configuration and shall not drive the SPI output lines.

The SPI transaction processing logic shall be held in reset when the primary chip select is inactive and shall become active when a transaction begins. This ensures each new SPI transaction starts from a defined state.

### 2.4 Alerts

The module shall assert an alert when a TL-UL bus integrity error is detected. Alert test capability shall be provided so software can exercise the alert path.

### 2.5 DFT and Scan Behavior

When scan or memory built-in self-test mode is enabled, the module shall accept external scan clock and reset controls. In these modes, the SPI clock is not required for internal operation.

### 2.6 Memory Configuration

The module shall apply the provided SRAM configuration input to its internal memory.

### 2.7 SPI Clock Monitoring

The module shall provide the SPI clock input to an external clock monitor output.

---

## 3. Generic SPI Mode

In generic mode, the module shall perform a raw, full-duplex serial-to-parallel and parallel-to-serial transfer. It shall not interpret the received byte stream as command or address information.

### 3.1 Receive Path

The module shall shift in data from the host-to-device data line on each active SPI clock edge, assemble bytes, and store them in the RX buffer portion of the internal SRAM.

Behavior requirements:

- Hardware shall maintain the RX write pointer. Software shall consume received data by updating the RX read pointer.
- The module shall expose the RX buffer fill level and empty/full status to software.
- If the RX buffer is full when a new byte completes, the byte shall be discarded and an RX overflow condition shall be reported.
- Partial data at the end of a transaction shall still be made available to software. If an aligned memory word has not been completed, the module shall flush the partial data after a software-configurable timeout.

### 3.2 Transmit Path

Software shall place transmit data into the TX buffer and advance the TX write pointer. Hardware shall read the data, serialize it, and drive it on the device-to-host data line on each active SPI clock edge.

Behavior requirements:

- Hardware shall update the TX read pointer as data is transmitted.
- The module shall expose the TX buffer depth and empty/full status.
- If no valid transmit data is available, the module shall continue to drive data to keep the SPI clock active. The driven value may be stale or repeated data. Software must preload or reset the transmit path before a transfer when deterministic idle data is required.
- A TX underflow condition shall be reported when the transmit data path is read while empty.

### 3.3 Generic-Mode Interrupts

The module shall generate interrupt requests for:

- RX buffer full,
- RX fill level at or above a configured watermark,
- TX fill level below a configured watermark,
- RX overflow,
- TX underflow.

The RX frame-error interrupt shall be present in the interrupt interface as a reserved condition and shall not be asserted in this implementation.

---

## 4. SPI Flash Mode

In SPI flash mode, the module shall behave as a serial flash device. It shall parse incoming SPI flash commands and respond according to the command information configured by software.

### 4.1 Command Information

The module shall maintain a list of command descriptions. Each command description shall define:

- whether the entry is valid,
- the opcode to match,
- the address width,
- whether address manipulation is enabled,
- whether dummy cycles are present and their length,
- whether payload is present, its direction, and byte count,
- whether payload manipulation is enabled,
- whether the command should be uploaded,
- whether the uploaded command should set the busy status bit.

The first command entries are dedicated to read status, JEDEC ID, SFDP, and read commands. Additional entries are available for software-defined commands, especially for command upload and passthrough control. Dedicated entries are also provided for EN4B/EX4B, write-enable, and write-disable commands.

When a command byte is received, the module shall compare it against the enabled command information and activate the corresponding behavior.

### 4.2 Flash Status Register

The module shall maintain a 3-byte flash status register containing:

- a busy bit,
- a write-enable-latch bit,
- software-controlled status bits.

The read status commands, using the configured status opcodes, shall return the status register contents on the device-to-host data line.

Behavior requirements:

- The busy bit shall be set by hardware when a command with the busy attribute is uploaded.
- Software shall clear the busy bit after completing the operation that set it.
- The write-enable-latch bit shall be set and cleared by hardware when the configured write-enable and write-disable opcodes are received. Software may also modify this bit.
- Software writes to the flash status register shall not affect an in-progress transaction. The new value shall take effect atomically after the current SPI transaction is deasserted, so that the host always reads a consistent status value.
- In passthrough mode, while the busy bit is set, the module shall block passthrough activity at the start of a transaction until software clears the busy bit.

### 4.3 JEDEC ID

The module shall recognize the configured JEDEC ID command and respond by returning the configured JEDEC ID data.

Behavior requirements:

- The response shall begin with the configured number of continuation-code bytes.
- The module shall then return the configured manufacturer and device ID in the defined order.
- The host may continue clocking data until chip select deasserts; the module shall continue providing data from the JEDEC response while the transaction remains active.

### 4.4 SFDP Read

The module shall recognize the configured SFDP read command.

Behavior requirements:

- The module shall accept a 24-bit address.
- The lower address bits shall select a byte within the 256-byte SFDP space.
- The module shall return SFDP data continuously until chip select deasserts.

### 4.5 Read Command Processing

The module shall support the configured read command opcodes, including normal read, fast read, and dual/quad output read variants.

Behavior requirements:

- The module shall accept a 3-byte or 4-byte address depending on the configured address mode and the current 4-byte address mode state.
- The address shall be received on the first SPI data line.
- If the command description specifies dummy cycles, the module shall wait for the configured number of cycles before driving data.
- After the address and dummy phase, the module shall return data from the read buffer on the appropriate SPI data lines according to the command type:
  - single output: data on the device-to-host line,
  - dual output: data on two data lines,
  - quad output: data on four data lines.
- Data shall continue to be returned until chip select deasserts.

### 4.6 Read Buffer Management

The read buffer space is organized as two 1 kB halves, providing a double-buffer scheme.

Behavior requirements:

- The module shall use the low-order address bits of the received read command to access the read buffer.
- The module shall capture the last read address and make it available to software after the transaction ends.
- Addresses used for mailbox or SFDP accesses shall not be reported as normal read-buffer addresses.
- The module shall generate a watermark event when the received read address crosses a software-configurable threshold within the current 1 kB buffer.
- The module shall generate a buffer-flip event when a read command crosses from one 1 kB buffer half to the other.
- Software is responsible for refilling the inactive buffer half.

### 4.7 Mailbox

The module shall provide a configurable mailbox region in the SRAM.

Behavior requirements:

- The mailbox base address shall be aligned to the mailbox buffer size.
- When mailbox mode is enabled and the received read address falls within the configured mailbox region, the module shall fetch data from the mailbox buffer instead of the normal read buffer.
- This mailbox redirect shall apply to read commands that would otherwise access the read buffer.

### 4.8 4-Byte Address Mode Tracking

The module shall support automatic switching between 3-byte and 4-byte address mode in response to the configured EN4B and EX4B opcodes.

Behavior requirements:

- When the EN4B opcode is received, the module shall switch the internal address mode to 4-byte addressing.
- When the EX4B opcode is received, the module shall switch the internal address mode to 3-byte addressing.
- The new address mode shall be broadcast to all affected behaviors for subsequent transactions.
- The updated address mode shall also be reflected in the software-visible configuration state after synchronization.
- The module shall ignore the remainder of the SPI transaction after recognizing an EN4B or EX4B opcode.

### 4.9 Command Upload

The module shall provide command upload for commands that are not processed entirely by dedicated hardware and whose command information entry has upload enabled.

Behavior requirements:

- The module shall store the received command byte in a command FIFO.
- If the command description includes an address, the decoded address shall be stored in an address FIFO.
- If the command description includes payload, the payload bytes shall be stored in a payload buffer.
- The module shall expose the command FIFO depth, address FIFO depth, payload depth, and payload start index to software.
- The module shall generate an interrupt when a command is stored in the command FIFO and when payload data becomes available.
- If the received payload exceeds the maximum payload buffer size, the module shall report a payload overflow condition. The payload data may wrap within the buffer; the payload start index shall indicate the location of the first valid byte.
- If the matched command information entry has the busy attribute set, the module shall set the flash status busy bit when the command is uploaded.

---

## 5. SPI Passthrough Mode

In passthrough mode, the module shall relay SPI transactions from the host side to a downstream interface. It shall also provide filtering, data manipulation, and internal command interception.

### 5.1 Normal Forwarding

For transactions that are not filtered and not intercepted, the module shall forward the transaction to the downstream interface, preserving the SPI protocol behavior including command, address, dummy cycles, payload, and read data direction.

The module shall control the SPI data-line output enables according to the command information. If no command information entry matches the received opcode, the module shall assume the command is a single-lane payload-in command for output-enable purposes.

### 5.2 Command Filtering

The module shall provide a 256-bit filter mask, with one bit per possible opcode.

Behavior requirements:

- If the received opcode has its corresponding filter bit set, the module shall suppress the transaction from being forwarded to the downstream interface.
- The module shall still allow the command to be captured by the upload logic if the matching command information entry has upload enabled.
- Filtered transactions shall not produce read data on the host interface.

### 5.3 Internal Interception

In passthrough mode, software may enable interception of selected command classes:

- read status,
- JEDEC ID,
- SFDP,
- mailbox read accesses.

Behavior requirements:

- When interception is enabled for a command class, the module shall process that command internally using the same behavior as in flash mode and shall not forward it downstream.
- The intercept configuration shall be stable during an active SPI transaction.
- For mailbox reads, the module shall intercept only when the received address falls into the configured mailbox region.

### 5.4 Address Manipulation

The module shall provide address bit manipulation for commands whose command information entry has address-swap enabled.

Behavior requirements:

- A configured address mask selects which address bits are affected.
- For each selected bit, the address bit shall be replaced with the corresponding value from the configured address data.
- Unselected address bits shall pass through unchanged.

### 5.5 Payload Manipulation

The module shall provide payload bit manipulation for commands whose command information entry has payload-swap enabled.

Behavior requirements:

- The manipulation shall apply to the first four payload bytes.
- A configured payload mask selects which payload bits are affected.
- For each selected bit, the payload bit shall be replaced with the corresponding value from the configured payload data.
- The first byte received from the host shall be treated as the least-significant byte of the configured manipulation data.

---

## 6. TPM over SPI Mode

The TPM function uses a dedicated active-low chip select. When enabled and selected by its chip select, the TPM function shall own the shared SPI data lines.

### 6.1 TPM Transaction Parsing

The module shall parse the incoming TPM transaction as follows:

- The first byte shall be treated as the TPM command byte.
- The following three bytes shall be treated as the 24-bit TPM address.
- The module shall store the command and address in a command/address FIFO for software, except in the managed-register read case described below.

### 6.2 TPM Read Transactions

For TPM read transactions, the module shall generate the TPM response on the device-to-host data line.

Behavior requirements:

- For reads that fall into the hardware-managed register space, and when hardware register return is enabled and the TPM mode is FIFO mode, the module shall return the managed register value without requiring software to provide data.
- For all other reads, the module shall place the command and address into the command/address FIFO and wait for software to provide data in the read FIFO.
- The module shall send the TPM-defined wait byte while it is not ready to return data.
- When data becomes available, the module shall send the TPM-defined start byte followed by the data bytes.
- The module shall continue sending data from the read FIFO until the transaction ends.

### 6.3 TPM Write Transactions

For TPM write transactions, the module shall place the command and address into the command/address FIFO and receive the payload into the write FIFO.

Behavior requirements:

- If the write FIFO is empty, the module shall send the start byte immediately and accept the payload.
- If the write FIFO is not empty, the module shall send the wait byte until the write FIFO becomes empty, then send the start byte and accept the payload.
- The module shall not accept payload bytes while the write FIFO is full.

### 6.4 Hardware-Managed TPM Registers

The module shall maintain software-readable/writable storage for the TPM return-by-hardware registers, including:

- TPM access registers for each locality,
- TPM status registers,
- TPM interrupt enable, vector, and status registers,
- TPM interface capability register,
- TPM vendor and device ID registers,
- TPM revision ID register.

Behavior requirements:

- The module shall use the received TPM address and the active locality information to select the appropriate return value.
- The module shall support five localities.
- If an invalid locality is received and the invalid-locality configuration is enabled, the module shall return the TPM-defined invalid value.
- In FIFO mode, the module may return hardware-managed register values directly.
- In CRB mode, the module shall not return hardware-managed registers directly. All reads shall be uploaded to software, and software shall provide the response through the read FIFO.
- When hardware register return is disabled by software, all reads shall be handled through the read FIFO.
- Software shall not update hardware-managed registers while the TPM chip select is active.

### 6.5 TPM FIFO Behavior

The module shall expose the following FIFOs to software:

- a command/address FIFO,
- a write FIFO for received TPM payload data,
- a read FIFO for software-provided TPM response data.

The module shall expose the depth and not-empty status of these FIFOs.

The module shall generate an interrupt request when the command/address FIFO becomes non-empty.

The TPM interrupt enable, status, and vector registers are software-managed. The module shall not generate a separate TPM interrupt output beyond the command/address FIFO notification.

---

## 7. Interrupt Summary

The module shall provide interrupt requests for the following events:

| Interrupt | Assertion Condition |
|---|---|
| Generic RX full | The RX buffer transitions to the full state. |
| Generic RX watermark | The RX buffer fill level reaches or exceeds the configured watermark. |
| Generic TX watermark | The TX buffer fill level falls below the configured watermark. |
| Generic RX error | Reserved; not asserted in this implementation. |
| Generic RX overflow | A received byte is discarded because the RX path is full. |
| Generic TX underflow | The transmit data path is read while empty. |
| Upload command FIFO not empty | A command is stored in the upload command FIFO. |
| Upload payload not empty | Received payload data becomes available in the payload buffer. |
| Upload payload overflow | Received payload exceeds the payload buffer capacity. |
| Read buffer watermark | A read command address crosses the configured watermark. |
| Read buffer flip | A read command crosses between the two 1 kB read buffer halves. |
| TPM command/address not empty | The TPM command/address FIFO becomes non-empty. |

All interrupt requests shall be maskable through the interrupt enable controls. An interrupt request shall remain asserted until software clears the corresponding interrupt status, and software shall be able to trigger each interrupt for testing.

---

## 8. Additional Behavioral Requirements

The module shall arbitrate between software and hardware access to the internal SRAM. Hardware accesses required for an active SPI transaction shall be able to proceed without protocol violation; software accesses may be delayed while hardware requires the memory.

The module shall provide status and configuration fields that cross clock domains in a synchronized manner. Software-visible status dependent on the SPI clock domain may therefore be delayed by synchronization latency.

The module shall not modify the contents of a passthrough transaction except when commanded filtering, interception, address manipulation, or payload manipulation is enabled.

When the SPI clock is stopped and chip select is deasserted, the module shall retain all software-visible configuration and buffered data.
